newsitem.title: USA: Strong Amoco Q4 lifted by energy prices.
newsitem.headline: Strong Amoco Q4 lifted by energy prices.

text.p: Amoco Corp reported record profits for the fourth quarter driven primarily by higher energy prices that made 1996 a banner year for most large U.S. energy companies.

The giant oil, natural gas and chemicals company said higher natural gas prices, in particular, boosted results. Natural gas prices increased almost $1.00 per thousand cubic feet compared to the fourth quarter of 1995, Amoco said.
"Higher prices for crude oil and natural gas, along with higher volumes and ongoing cost containment efforts, contributed to 1996's record performance," Amoco said.
While earnings from the company's exploration and production sectors rose in the United States, Canada and overseas, earnings from its chemicals sector declined.
Earnings from its petroleum products sector rose as well, but refined product margins were squeezed by higher crude oil costs, the company said.

"Our business continues to grow outside North America with significant 1996 discoveries in Trinidad, Egypt and Venezuela. For the fourth consecutive year we also expect to more than replace annual production," Amoco chairman and chief executive Laurance Fuller said in a statement.

Worldwide capital and exploration spending in 1996 was $4.6 billion, excluding the first-quarter acquisition of Albemarle Corp's alpha-olefins and related businesses for about $500 million, compared to $4.1 billion in 1995.

The 1997 capital investment and exploration program of $4.1 billion excludes $307 million for expenses related to a recently approved 50 percent involvement in a new Bolivian oil and gas company, Empresa Petrolera Chaco, the company said.
Fourth-quarter U.S. exploration and production earnings were $393 million, up from $174 million before a $234-million impairment charge in the year-ago period, Amoco said.
"The fourth-quarter 1996 earnings improvement reflected higher crude oil and natural gas prices, increased natural gas volumes and lower exploration expenses," Amoco said.

Canadian exploration and production earnings for the quarter were $154 million, versus $33 million a year earlier excluding a $93 million impairments charge. Improved results reflected "significantly higher natural gas liquid margins and sales volumes, increased energy prices and lower exploration expenses," the company said.

Overseas exploration and production earnings were $141 million on the quarter, compared to $94 million a year ago, reflecting "higher crude oil and natural gas prices and increased crude oil sales volumes," Amoco said, adding that the gains were partly offset by higher exploration costs.

Petroleum products operations earned $61 million on the quarter, excluding a $90 million gain on an adjustment in LIFO inventory levels, compared with year-ago earnings of $54 million before a one-time gain of $83 million on the sale of Amoco Motor Club and an $11 million impairment charge.

U.S. refined product sales on the quarter totalled 1.237 million barrels per day, compared to 1.235 million barrels per day in the year-ago quarter. Refineries ran at 96 percent of rated capacity on the quarter, versus 93 percent a year ago.
The company said chemicals sector earnings for the fourth quarter were $105 million, down from $188 million, including a $42 million impairment charge, in the fourth quarter of 1995.

"Current quarter results were affected by significantly lower margins for olefins, reflecting higher feedstock costs, and softened paraxylene margins, due to lower prices," Amoco said. "Partly offsetting were investment incentives, and higher sales volumes along the paraxylene and purified terephthalic acid chain."

Shares in Amoco were up 1/4 to 85-1/4 after the company said total earnings for the year were $2.83 billion, or $5.69 per share, versus $1.86 billion, or $3.76 per share, in 1995. Annual revenues topped $36.07 billion, up from $31 billion.
